No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

```sh

git fetch origin 3bd4a20994cb28b8052abb5af100e05855f15863 && git checkout 3bd4a20994cb28b8052abb5af100e05855f15863
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 31ce45c071bbcb6e92a730ce19ebf30dcfa361cb cca354048165cb46cdbfb3d1a55401b636bcc1b1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 31ce45c071bbcb6e92a730ce19ebf30dcfa361cb && git merge --no-ff cca354048165cb46cdbfb3d1a55401b636bcc1b1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 31ce45c071bbcb6e92a730ce19ebf30dcfa361cb
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The ceremony refusal — holds.**
- Refuses before any read or write. The registered command is now `MigrateOrganizationOwnership extends OrganizationOwnershipCeremony` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts:1123`); its `run()` (`:1128-1145`) does `this.parse(...)` and nothing else before refusing. Every ceremony flag is `Flags.string` / `Flags.boolean` with no `exists` or custom `parse` (`:320-395`); the only environment read is `OS_DATABASE_URL` for `--database-url`, so parse touches no file and no database. No `resolveTenancyPosture()`, no supplement or plan-file read, no `probeMigrationTarget`, no `bootSchemaStack`. Under `--json`, `emitJson({ error: plan_refused | apply_refused, reason: 'upgrade-unavailable', code: 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED', detail }, 1, { compact: true })` writes the payload and sets `process.exitCode = 1` (`utils/format.ts:304-311`); otherwise `printError(...)` then `this.exit(1)`. The release-refusal pin stubs the boot and the probe to throw, sets an unrecognised posture and missing files, and asserts no db or out file appears.
- ADR-0112 code: the standard `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (`:1115`); no spec, ledger or docs regeneration touched. The message (`:1110-1112`) names "18.0", "fresh installs only", "an 18.x release", "Keep a v17 database on a 17.x release", "Nothing was read or written".
- Class kept whole. `OrganizationOwnershipCeremony` (`:319`) is the former default class renamed; the only change inside it is its own `this.parse(OrganizationOwnershipCeremony)` self-reference. The subclass overrides `description` and `run()` only; `flags` is inherited by identity (pinned). 18.x restores the ceremony by deleting `:1095-1146` and re-adding `default` to `:319` — one step, no flag to remove.
- No bypass. `os dev`'s automatic ceremony (`utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts:85-96`) spawns the real binary, `[binPath, 'migrate', 'organization-ownership', '--dev', ...]`, so it receives this refusal and reports it (`:149`, "The upgrade plan was refused, and nothing was changed"). It runs only from `coordinator.recover` when the `serve --dev` child has sent `objectstack:organization-ownership-required` (`commands/dev.ts:767`, `:815-835`), which the boot guard emits only for a v17-shaped database or an unverified marker; a fresh database (`tables.length === 0 && marker === 'absent'`) is never refused, so on a fresh database the ceremony never runs. On a v17 development database the helper copies the file into the backups directory before it spawns the plan (`:131-134`); the copy and a `ceremony.log` are written, the database is not. The only other non-test importer of the ceremony's utils is `commands/migrate/apply.ts:45`, which imports the drop gate solely to REFUSE `--allow-destructive` drops of `organization_id` until the ceremony's marker is verified — it runs no ceremony step, and in 18.0 the marker can never be verified, so those drops stay refused (D10 item 5 kept). No importer of the module outside `packages/cli` except the dogfood test.

**(b) The walled-boot refusal at `os serve` — holds.**
- Narrowest operator entry: `os dev` spawns `serve --dev` (`commands/dev.ts:736-741`), `os start` spawns `serve` (`commands/start.ts:524-528`), so `serve.ts:2419-2423` is the single funnel for all three CLI boots. It sits immediately after `resolveTenancyPostureOrRefusal()` and before `isDevelopmentBoot` / `anchorServedApp` (the config path): before a config is read, a plugin is mounted or the kernel bootstraps. Ahead of it run only `this.parse`, the stdout reservation, the port probe and `loadProjectEnvFiles` (necessarily — the posture lives in `.env`); the FATAL's statements ("No config has been loaded, no plugin has been mounted, the HTTP server was never started") are true.
- Same reading as the runtime: the gate wraps `resolveTenancyPosture()` from `@objectstack/types` (`types/src/env.ts:147-164`: `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE` normalised, else `OS_MULTI_ORG_ENABLED` ⇒ `isolated` / `single`), the same function `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:2225`, `plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts:661`, and `objectql/src/registry.ts:2316` call; the walled set is `postureEnforcesWall` from `@objectstack/spec/security`, the runtime's own predicate. `walledPostureRefusal` (`serve.ts:6266-6285`) re-reads the environment only to NAME the source in the message.
- Escape hatch: none. `walledPostureRefusal(posture)` consults no flag and no variable for its verdict; `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY` is read only downstream (`serve.ts:4373+`), and both e2e files pin that it does not lift the refusal. Refused via `process.exit(1)`, like the sibling gate, so no `catch` can demote it.
- Kernel-level and dogfood walled fixtures: `@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack`, `createStandaloneStack`, the five `packages/qa/dogfood/test/wall-*.dogfood.test.ts`, plugin-auth's walled-owner tests never pass through `serve`; none is touched by the diff.
- The two e2e rewrites (−191): all seven deleted cases boot the real `os serve` process under `SERVE_ENV.OS_TENANCY_POSTURE: 'isolated'` (`host-resolution:179-186`, `mount-failure:168-175`), so every one is a walled `os serve` boot 18.0 refuses. What they covered: a walled boot reaching the banner with the package in the app; the ADR-0093 D5 absent-package fail-fast and the #4719 NODE_PATH shim; the degraded boot under the hatch; the #4818 import-vs-mount classification and the hatch not swallowing a mount refusal. What stays live: the message sites 3–5 (D5 fatal, degraded warning, mount refusal) in-process in `serve-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts`; the #4719 host-root resolution rule in `serve-config-plugin-host-resolution.test.ts` and `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts`; the wall and the degraded state at kernel level in `plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.test.ts:36,139` ("degraded: isolated requested but isolation NOT active", never guesses) and the dogfood wall suites. The organizations-runtime classification over a real process is the one thing with no live coverage, and it is unreachable code in 18.0. Acceptable: the fixtures (`writeApp`, `writeOrganizationsPackage`, `runServe`) are kept, the new cases pin that neither stage runs, and both headers name the restore point. Flagged under ③ as an obligation on the 18.x PR.
- Other operator entries that still boot walled in 18.0 — named, as the scope is "the operator's boot path": (i) the one-shot kernel boots of the `os migrate` family, `os secret rewrap` / `orphans`, `os storage orphans` and `os verify` (`bootSchemaStack` / `createStandaloneStack` / `bootStack`, 23 command files) open the database under whatever posture is set and are not refused; they serve no request. (ii) An embedded host — `createStandaloneStack` / `createDefaultHostConfig`, documented at `content/docs/deployment/single-project-mode.mdx:85-100`, and `@objectstack/adapter-hono` — boots walled unrefused. Plan amendment 14 offered `serve` / `dev` / `start` OR the runtime host and ranked keeping the kernel-level walled fixtures above a wider refusal; a refusal at `createStandaloneStack` is exactly the hard-blocker case it named. So (ii) is inside the ruled latitude, and the single-project-mode page makes no posture claim, so no doc is false. Both are boundary flags, not blocks.

**(c) `single` unchanged — holds.** `walledPostureRefusal('single')` answers `null` (`postureEnforcesWall` false), pinned with its ablation (A3); nothing else in `serve.ts` changes. The boot guard (`runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`) is untouched and never refuses a fresh database. A fresh `single` install boots and serves exactly as before.

**(d) The 16 test-file import changes — hold.** Each swaps `default` for `OrganizationOwnershipCeremony` while keeping the local name `MigrateOrganizationOwnership` (two lines where a `type Command` alias exists), so every assertion body is byte-identical and the ceremony's coverage is kept, not weakened. The dogfood file moves step 2 from the binary to the ceremony class in its own process (oclif auto-transpile off, as `bin/run.js` does) and adds step 2a, in which the binary refuses with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, writes no plan file, and `sys_metadata`'s columns are unchanged. What the suite no longer proves — that the REGISTERED command runs the ceremony — is the narrowing itself, and the release-refusal pin's fifth case proves the registered class is the ceremony's subclass with its flags and a different `run`.

**(e) Docs — true and minimal.** `cli.mdx` (the `os dev` upgrade callout `:206-209`, the table row `:1205`, the command callout `:1484-1489`), `environment-variables.mdx:101`, `self-hosting.mdx:469-470`, `tenancy-modes.mdx:19-22`: one sentence each, each true against the code (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, exit 1, `code` beside `error` under `--json`, `os serve` and so `os dev` / `os start` refuse `group` and `isolated` before a config is read). One looseness, not a falsity: `cli.mdx:207` "stops at step 2 ... and changes nothing" — step 1's backup copy and log are written on a v17 development database; the database is not changed, and "stops at step 2" says step 1 ran. Nothing under `content/docs/releases/` is touched (file list; the docs-drift bot's four release pages are read-only hits on the literal `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/15212-180-guards-fresh-single-only.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': minor` — the launch-window level for a breaking change (AGENTS.md § Post-Task Checklist 3; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`). The body carries `**BREAKING**` and `feat(cli)!:`, and states each narrowing as a `**FROM** … **TO** …` pair with a one-line `**Fix:**` (stay on 17.x; `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=single` or unset both variables), plus a "What stays as it was" paragraph. The AGENTS.md FROM → TO rule binds only a removal or rename of something an author can write; this change removes none, and the changeset states the pairs anyway.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and its claim is a positive fact, not a detector miss: no spec key, export, config field or error code is removed or renamed (`MigrateOrganizationOwnership` stays the default export; the new exports are additions; `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` already exists). The two pairs are operator-behaviour mappings with operator remedies, not consumer-code rewrites — the shape the gate's framing detector is built to leave alone. Gates: Check Changeset ✓, Lint · CI, release & engine gates ✓ (`check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`).
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: a valid spelling and the right arm. `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; `reviewFace` maps ANY `(narrowing)` arm, `yes (narrowing)` included, to the narrowing face at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (`record-recognisers.mjs:187-188, :238`). The claim pre-measured `no (narrowing)`; the dev's `yes` is defensible — the `--json` refusal payload gains a new `reason` value (`upgrade-unavailable`) and a `code` key, and the command's description gains a prefix — and either value lands at `minor` on this face. The PR body and the changeset carry the same line. Not blocking.
- `Part of #15212`: right. #15212 carries plan amendment 14 and the claim for `claude/issue-15212-180-guards`; the gates "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" and "Part-of PR must not also close its card" are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Check-runs on the head at review time: 33 success, 5 skipped (opt-in / matrix placeholders), 2 in progress — `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record judges the contract and does not stand in for them. The merge waits for both.

The report's open questions:
1. Where the refusal sits — A (`os serve`'s gate) is right, for the reasons in ① (b). The two boot classes it does not reach are named there: the `os migrate` / `os verify` one-shot kernel boots and embedded hosts (`createStandaloneStack`, `adapter-hono`). Both are inside plan amendment 14's latitude; the seat should carry (ii) into the D14 dated note on #24422 so the 18.0 scope statement reads "the `os` boot path", not "every boot".
2. The refusing subclass over a kept ceremony class — right; no flag.
3. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` — right; no vocabulary member for a temporary state. The docs-drift bot's rows on the literal are advisory.
4. The boot guard's prescription — escalated to the seat, not blocking. On a v17 database the guard names a command that refuses, and the refusal says to stay on 17.x: the chain terminates loudly and correctly, but in two hops. B (one sentence in `organizationOwnershipRefusalMessage`, `runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts:211-240`) is a runtime-package change outside this stage's claimed surface; recommend a one-line follow-up card on the 18.0 list, or a rider on C11 (#15214).

The report's out-of-scope findings:
1. `TENANCY_POSTURE_FIX_HINTS` (`cli/src/utils/tenancy-posture-hints.ts:135-141`) still offers `group` / `isolated` as fixes for an unrecognised posture — following either reaches this PR's loud refusal on the next boot. Acceptable for 18.0; a one-line hint is a candidate rider for C11.
2. `os doctor` reports a walled posture without the 18.0 sentence — the next `os serve` refuses loudly. Acceptable; same C11 rider.
3. Embedded hosts are not refused — answered under open question 1: inside the ruled latitude, and the right trade against the kernel-level walled suites. Name it in the D14 note.

Obligation on the 18.x restore, so it is not lost: delete the subclass (`organization-ownership.ts:1095-1146`); delete the `walledPostureRefusal` call and function (`serve.ts:2411-2423, :6255-6285`); restore the seven e2e cases of `serve-organizations-host-resolution.e2e.test.ts` and `serve-organizations-mount-failure.e2e.test.ts` from the parent of this PR's squash commit, in the same landing; put dogfood step 2 back on the binary and drop step 2a; remove the six docs sentences. Recommend the seat opens the 18.x card with this list now.
